record.context_brief: Specialization ranks in families of abelian varieties
record.original_question: Suppose X is a curve over a field of characteristic 0 and π: A → X is an abelian scheme over X. Let Γ be a group of sections of π, and assume that no element of Γ factors through a subfamily of group varieties of relative dimension 1. For a geometric point P in X(ḱ), let Γ_P denote the fiber of Γ above P. Must there be only finitely many points P for which rank(Γ_P)=rank(Γ)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$ with algebraic closure $\bar k$. Let $X$ be a smooth irreducible curve over $k$, and let $\pi\colon \mathcal{A}\to X$ be an abelian scheme. Denote by $\mathcal{A}(X)$ the group of sections of $\pi$, and let $\Gamma\subseteq \mathcal{A}(X)$ be a finitely generated subgroup. Assume that no nonzero element of $\Gamma$ factors through an abelian subscheme of $\mathcal{A}\to X$ whose fibers are of relative dimension one (equivalently, $\Gamma$ has no nonzero element lying in a one-dimensional abelian subscheme of $\mathcal{A}$ over $X$). 

For each geometric point $P\in X(\bar k)$, let $\Gamma_P\subseteq \mathcal{A}_P(\bar k)$ denote the image of $\Gamma$ under the specialization map $\sigma_P\colon \mathcal{A}(X)\to \mathcal{A}_P(\bar k)$ at $P$, and write $\mathrm{rank}(\Gamma_P)$ for the rank of $\Gamma_P$ as a finitely generated abelian group. By Silverman's specialization theorem one has $\mathrm{rank}(\Gamma_P)\ge \mathrm{rank}(\Gamma)$ for all but finitely many $P$.

Prove or disprove: there are only finitely many points $P\in X(\bar k)$ for which 
$$\mathrm{rank}(\Gamma_P)=\mathrm{rank}(\Gamma).$$ 
Equivalently, for all but finitely many $P\in X(\bar k)$ one has $\mathrm{rank}(\Gamma_P)>\mathrm{rank}(\Gamma)$.
artifact.category_tag: Specialization of ranks in families of abelian varieties
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a sharpening of Silverman's specialization theorem in families of abelian varieties over curves in characteristic 0, closely related to the circle of "unlikely intersections" results of Masser–Zannier and the relative Manin–Mumford / Pink–Zannier conjectures. General results of this strength (showing the rank strictly jumps at all but finitely many specializations, under a non-isotriviality / no-one-dimensional-factor hypothesis) do not appear in the literature; recent surveys and papers on specialization maps and unlikely intersections treat it as an open problem, with partial results in low dimensions and under additional hypotheses.

status_evidence.title: Specialization Maps and Unlikely Intersections (Silverman)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses how often rank(Γ_P) equals rank(Γ) for sections of abelian schemes over curves; connections with unlikely intersections.
status_evidence.claim: The expected statement that the rank stays equal to the generic rank only at finitely many points is presented as a conjecture/open question.

status_evidence.title: The relative Manin–Mumford conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Studies specialization of sections in abelian schemes over curves, following Pila–Zannier; results are conditional or partial.
status_evidence.claim: Related specialization questions for sections in families of abelian varieties remain partially open.
